Holly O'Connell

Manager (CEO, Engine Room Records, LLC)

  1. The Band
  2. Holly O'Connell

The "Anchor". Holly (Age 18 in 1987) is the most formidable member of The Stardust Engine, and she has never played a note on stage. An academic prodigy, she entered a Dual Enrollment program at age 16—attending Blacksburg High School in the mornings and riding Blue Ridge Transit Route 1 onto the Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) campus every afternoon to take undergraduate business and commercial law courses alongside her older siblings and cousins.

While still dual-enrolled in high school and CPI, she took on the role of the band's manager at the Progress Street house. Her official role was to act as the emotional peacemaker—famously pulling Ryan and Cassidy into a "three-way hug" when they argued over music, reminding them "You're both right. And you're both idiots."

The First Redline: The 1986 CPI Mutual Cross-License

Holly's first legal masterstroke happened at the Progress Street kitchen table in October 1986, when she was a sixteen-year-old dual-enrolled high school junior taking afternoon undergraduate courses in Business Administration and Commercial Contract Law at CPI. When Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler prepared to submit their cassette demo of "Ignition (The Forger's Call)" to the CPI Student Government Association's football anthem contest, Holly—with her CPI Commercial Contracts textbook open right next to her high school binder—read the fine print on the back of the entry form. Buried in Paragraph 4 was a standard boilerplate "Work Made for Hire" clause that would have permanently signed away 100% of the band's master and publishing rights to the CPI Athletic Foundation.

Refusing to let her family lose their song, Holly took a red pen to the entry form and marched into the Office of University Counsel. She negotiated a historic $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License: The Stardust Engine kept 100% of their master and publishing rights while granting CPI Athletics and the Marching Forgers a perpetual, royalty-free stadium and broadcast synchronization license to play "Ignition" (and future Stardust Engine stadium anthems) inside The Crucible. In exchange, CPI's Office of Trademarks & Licensing granted the band (and any label they wholly owned) a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free Co-Existence & Artistic Reference License to use the institutional marks CPI, Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute, The Forgers, and The Crucible across their songs, album titles, and liner notes—a clause Holly pulled from the vault eighteen years later in October 2004 to stage the secret fourth-quarter stadium debut of "Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible" forty-eight hours before Progress Street dropped.

The Crash of '90: "The Gatekeeper"

When Ryan was paralyzed in December 1990, Holly's role expanded from Business Manager to Medical Director. She holds Durable Power of Attorney for Ryan, giving her the legal authority to make medical decisions in an emergency. She carries signed, notarized HIPAA release forms in her briefcase at all times.

The "Friction" Nuke (1992)

Holly's true power was revealed during the 1992 "Friction" scandal. By this time, she was a 2L law student. When Julian Vance made his criminal demand, Holly transformed into "Holly the Shark". She secured the evidence that forced Apex Records to surrender the masters, using the freedom to found Engine Room Records, LLC.

CONFIDENTIAL: The "American Dream" Event (1996)

The Financial Architect

In 1996, when Cassidy handed her the winning lottery ticket worth $2.04 Billion, Holly didn't celebrate. She went to work.

"Money destroys families," she famously said. To prevent that, she spent the next two decades armoring herself with every credential available. She created the Forger Nation Trust, a structure that renders the band members "penniless" on paper—protecting them from lawsuits—while the Trust manages their empire.

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
